title: Eggs Benedict
subtitle: Poached eggs with hollandaise on English muffin and ham
excerpt: The classic brunch dish done properly: perfectly poached eggs and good-quality ham on toasted English muffins, blanketed in a rich, buttery hollandaise sauce. The hollandaise is the challenge and the reward.

recipe.sourceNotes: Eggs Benedict is a classic American brunch dish, disputed in origin but generally attributed to New York restaurants of the late nineteenth century. The dish consists of poached eggs served on toasted English muffins with back bacon or ham and covered with hollandaise sauce. The hollandaise sauce is an emulsion of clarified butter whisked into egg yolks that have been reduced with white wine vinegar; it is one of the five French mother sauces. Hollandaise is temperature-sensitive: too hot and the eggs scramble, breaking the sauce; too cold and the butter solidifies. The target temperature is 63 to 65°C. The sauce should be made just before serving as it does not hold well.

content.text: Make the hollandaise first, keep it warm in a bowl over hot (not simmering) water, and poach the eggs last. If the hollandaise splits, whisk in a teaspoon of cold water off the heat; this often rescues it. The eggs are ready when the whites are fully set but the yolks are completely liquid.

items.preparation: 2 for poaching; 2 yolks for the hollandaise
thick slices; toasted; or English muffins

content.text: Make the hollandaise: reduce 2 tbsp white wine vinegar with a splash of water in a small pan until 1 tbsp remains. Cool slightly. Whisk 2 egg yolks into the reduction in a heatproof bowl over barely simmering water. Whisk until pale, thick, and doubled. Remove from the heat. Slowly drizzle in the clarified butter, whisking constantly, to make a thick, emulsified sauce. Season with lemon, salt, and white pepper. Keep warm.

Bring a deep pan of water to a gentle simmer. Add 1 tbsp vinegar. Create a gentle vortex, crack in one egg at a time, and poach for 3 minutes until the whites are just set. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Assemble immediately: place a split toasted muffin on each plate, top with the warmed ham, then the poached egg. Spoon the hollandaise generously over the top. Season. Serve at once.
